## Introduction

> For this assignment, our group created a shared Zotero library to collect and organize research for our Culminating Experience Project. Zotero gives us one place to save citation details, articles, notes, and tags, and it will make it easier for us to return to these sources once we begin writing our project report.

Our topic centers on generative AI in advertising and marketing, with a particular focus on how AI-generated content like images, ads, and marketing communication shapes consumer trust, attitudes, and purchase behavior, and how that plays out specifically in fashion and luxury contexts[^1].

[^1]: This document was prepared in Quarto and rendered to a self-contained HTML file per the assignment's submission requirements.

## Group Zotero Library {#sec-library}

Our shared library is called **IBM CEP Bibliography Database**. Each group member added and organized sources related to the project, and the screenshot below shows the library name along with the articles added so far.

## Example Zotero Item {#sec-item}

Figure @sec-item shows one completed item from the library. The entry includes the article's citation information, DOI, a short note explaining its relevance, and tags that make it easier to find later.

::: callout-tip
## What this screenshot show

-   Citation information (authors, title, publication, year, etc.)
-   Attached PDF, snapshot, or URL
-   Notes
-   Tags
:::

![](images/CEP01imageszotero-group-library%202.png){fig-align="center"}

::: callout-note
The example article focuses on how Gen Z female consumers respond to AI-generated fashion advertisements. The item is tagged with terms related to generative AI, fashion advertising, Gen Z, and consumer perception.
:::

The findings help identify conditions under which AI-generated advertisements may be accepted or viewed negatively. | AI-generated advertising; consumer attitudes; consumer trust |
